ap_statistics-f01.title: A blocked experiment comparing two fertilizers for tomato plants

stimulus.description: Summary of the height after eight weeks for each treatment group.

data.notes: Results for the two treatment groups of 48 tomato plants, with the blocks combined.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: A researcher plans an experiment to compare two fertilizers, Fertilizer A and Fertilizer B, using $48$ tomato plants. The researcher will record the height after eight weeks of each plant. Identify (i) the experimental units and (ii) the response variable.
parts.model_answer: (i) The experimental units are the $48$ tomato plants. (ii) The response variable is the height after eight weeks (centimeters).

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the experimental units as the 48 tomato plants (the individuals that receive a treatment)
alt_solutions: an equivalent statement in the student's own words that keeps the same meaning and the context
common_errors: names the treatments as the units
names the blocks as the units
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning in the context of the problem, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase. A response that states the right conclusion without the stated reason, or a reason without the conclusion, earns this row only when the row asks for just one of them.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies the response variable as the height after eight weeks
alt_solutions: an equivalent statement in the student's own words that keeps the same meaning and the context
common_errors: names the explanatory variable (the fertilizer) as the response
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning in the context of the problem, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase. A response that states the right conclusion without the stated reason, or a reason without the conclusion, earns this row only when the row asks for just one of them.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: The researcher decides to block the tomato plants by the greenhouse bench (sunny or shady). (i) Explain the purpose of blocking in this experiment. (ii) Describe how to assign the treatments at random within the blocks.
parts.model_answer: (i) Blocking groups tomato plants that are alike in amount of sunlight, so the treatments are compared within similar units and variability due to amount of sunlight is removed from the comparison. (ii) Within each block separately, randomly assign half of the tomato plants to Fertilizer A and the other half to Fertilizer B, for example by drawing names or using random numbers.

rubric_rows.criterion: Explains that blocking compares the treatments among similar units so that variability due to the blocking variable (amount of sunlight) does not hide or confuse the effect of the treatments
required_elements: controls variability from the blocking variable
alt_solutions: each treatment appears in every block so the blocking variable cannot explain a difference
common_errors: says blocking makes the sample random
says blocking removes the need for random assignment
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning in the context of the problem, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase. A response that states the right conclusion without the stated reason, or a reason without the conclusion, earns this row only when the row asks for just one of them.

rubric_rows.criterion: Describes random assignment carried out separately within each block, with about half of the units in each block receiving each treatment
required_elements: half of each block to each treatment
alt_solutions: shuffle the names in each block and give the first half one treatment
common_errors: randomly assigns across all units ignoring the blocks
assigns the treatments by choice of the units
rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning in the context of the problem, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase. A response that states the right conclusion without the stated reason, or a reason without the conclusion, earns this row only when the row asks for just one of them.

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: The table shown gives the results for each treatment group, with the blocks combined. Calculate the difference in the mean height after eight weeks, Fertilizer A minus Fertilizer B.
parts.model_answer: $72.1 - 67.5 = 4.6$ centimeters.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the difference in the means (answer 4.6 centimeters, with the subtraction in the stated order)
common_errors: subtracts in the opposite order
divides instead of subtracts

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Compare the distributions of the height after eight weeks for the two treatment groups, using the means and the standard deviations in the table. Your comparison should address both center and spread, in context.
parts.model_answer: The mean height after eight weeks is about $4.6$ centimeters greater for Fertilizer A ($72.1$) than for Fertilizer B ($67.5$). The responses under Fertilizer B are more variable: the standard deviation is $4.5$ centimeters, compared with $2.8$ centimeters for Fertilizer A.

rubric_rows.criterion: Compares the centers in context: the mean height after eight weeks is greater for Fertilizer A than for Fertilizer B

common_errors: compares the groups without naming the response or the treatments
reverses the direction of the difference

A response that states the right conclusion without the stated reason, or a reason without the conclusion, earns this row only when the row asks for just one of them.

rubric_rows.criterion: Compares the spreads in context: the standard deviation is greater for Fertilizer B ($4.5$) than for Fertilizer A ($2.8$), so its responses are more variable
alt_solutions: an equivalent statement in the student's own words that keeps the same meaning and the context
common_errors: says the group with the greater mean is more variable

rubric_rows.grading_note: Award the point when the response conveys the required meaning in the context of the problem, whatever the wording; do not require any specific phrase. A response that states the right conclusion without the stated reason, or a reason without the conclusion, earns this row only when the row asks for just one of them.

parts.model_answer: (i) $\hat y = 19.29 + 2.65x$. (ii) When the advertising spending is $0$, the predicted sales is 19.29 thousand units. This is not meaningful, because $0$ is outside the range of the data (3 to 14 thousand dollars), so the interpretation would be an extrapolation.
